answer.rationale: memory_44 (enterprise sales-assisted flows) scores highest because enterprise deals typically have longer LTV and stickier retention, directly supporting sustainable long-term revenue. memory_31 (signup simplification for SMB) scores 4 because improved activation is a leading indicator of engagement and retention. memory_57 (referral incentives) scores 4 because referral channels tend to deliver high-quality, organic customers with better unit economics. memory_86 and memory_91 (onboarding/activation messaging) score 3 each—they improve activation metrics but lack evidence of impact on long-term retention, churn, or revenue durability. memory_73 (promotional pricing for SMB) scores lowest at 2 because while it may solve immediate acquisition shortfall, tactical discounting typically attracts price-sensitive accounts with poor retention and does not support sustainable long-term revenue; it also directly contradicts the current competitive threat (competitor undercutting on price). Given the current crisis (activation down 6%, completion down 4%, competitive pricing pressure), memory_73 appears to be the least reliable guide to sustainable growth.
